newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: India, Pakistan set agenda for peace talks.
newsitem.headline: India, Pakistan set agenda for peace talks.

text.p: India and Pakistan, seeking to put 50 years of rivalry and war behind them, on Monday announced an agenda and negotiating mechanism for future peace talks. A joint statement issued after weekend talks between the Indian and Pakistani foreign ministry secretaries, or top career diplomats, said the agenda included the long-running dispute over the divided Himalayan state of Jammu and Kashmir.
The agenda, which the statement said addressed "all outstanding issues of concern to both sides" covers "peace and security, including CBMs (confidence-building measures)".

The two countries, which have fought three wars since independence from Britain in 1947, also plan to discuss their military stand-off on the Siachen Glacier, terrorism and drug trafficking, and economic and commercial cooperation.

The statement followed talks that started on Friday between delegations led by foreign ministry secretaries Shamshad Ahmad of Pakistan and Salman Haider of India, which it said had been held in a "cordial and constructive atmosphere".
"It was also agreed that both sides would take all possible steps to prevent hostile propaganda and provocative actions against each other," the statement said.
It said the foreign secretaries would hold a third round of talks in September in New Delhi. The first ice-breaking session took place in the Indian capital in late March.
In a separate statement, the two sides said they had agreed to release Indian and Pakistani fishermen and boats detained for straying into each other's territorial waters.
They agreed to free 26 Pakistani boats and 195 crew and 35 Indian boats and 194 crew. "Other boats and crew will be released as and when identified," the joint statement said.
"I am happy to state that we have successfully completed the first stage of the task entrusted to us by our two prime ministers," Ahmad told a joint news conference.

"As you will note, the two sides have agreed to address all outstanding issues with a view to achiving the goal of good neighbourly and cooperative relations," he said. "We hope the mechanism on which we have agreed will initiate progress towards the settlement of all outstanding issues listed in the joint statement.

"On our part, we will continue the dialogue with sincerity and serious purpose. We have no illusions about the complexity of the work ahead of us. "It is important for both sides now to take steps to create conditions conducive to make the process purposeful and result-oriented," Ahmad added.
His Indian counterpart said the agreement "provides the basis for comprehensive, constructive and sustained dialogue between India and Pakistan".
"It is our purpose that the dialogue leads to establishment of trust, friendship and cooperation between the two countries," Haider said.
